Role this software plays in the analytical workflow.
Role or purpose of this tool in the method.
Name of the software (e.g. "Probe for EPMA").
URL to the software product or documentation.

1.description: Role of this material in the method.
Publication reference for the standard's accepted values.
Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).
The registry the schema:termCode belongs to (GeoReM, NIST SRM catalogue, USGS RM list).
Name of the material (e.g. "San Carlos olivine").
Registry code for the material on the schema:DefinedTerm path (e.g. "SRM 610", "ATHO-G").

2.description: How this column maps into the variableMeasured JSON-LD structure.
Default value for this column (pre-filled per row).

Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this column. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).
URI identifying this column's parameter type in a formal vocabulary. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).
true = constant across all target species (read-only column).
true = must be provided for every target-species row.

3.description: specify the quality measure that is reported, by name, with an ID ref, or as a Defined Term
the reported result of the quality measure, as a string, a number, or a defined term from a vocabulary

4.description:
Role of the related resource. Present only on a link that expresses a relationship; a plain labeled link such as a license omits it.
DCAT's declared range is dcat:Role (dcat.ttl: rdfs:range dcat:Role, and dcat:Role rdfs:subClassOf skos:Concept), so the DCAT-native form is a node typed dcat:Role. That form was NOT accepted here before 2026-10-01: this property was cdifConceptOrTermOrString alone, which matches a bare string, a sealed @id reference, a schema:DefinedTerm or a skos:Concept -- none of which a dcat:Role-typed node satisfies, because JSON Schema does no subclass reasoning.
dcat:Role is added as a branch rather than replacing the others, so the DCAT-native form becomes valid without invalidating anything already written. Note this leaves CDIF LOOSER than DCAT, deliberately: DCAT's range is dcat:Role alone, and CDIF also accepts a plain skos:Concept, a DefinedTerm, an @id reference and a string. That is the same both-forms stance taken on dcterms:relation, and it is a choice rather than an oversight -- do not read the extra branches as something not yet tightened.

The related resource -- the DCAT canonical pointer to what is being related to, which is distinct from schema:url, the presentation URL of the link itself.
An @id reference is the RECOMMENDED form and a string is permitted, which is DCMI's own position: "Recommended practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a string conforming to a formal identification system may be provided." DCMI declares no rdfs:range for this property, and of the 13 DCMI properties carrying an "intended to be used with non-literal values" restriction, this is deliberately not one. dcat.ttl does not re-declare or constrain it at all -- the only triple mentioning it in the whole DCAT vocabulary is `dcat:distribution rdfs:subPropertyOf dcterms:relation`.
So objectReference-only would be stricter than both DCAT and DCMI and would reject a form the specification sanctions. The anyOf matches how schema:additionalType is handled here: both forms valid, the object form used in examples and required only where a `contains` pins a specific value.
It was string-only until 2026-10-01, which rejected the @id form outright. Reported from outside by a PSDI validator taking a things-not-strings approach (profile-core#16): their DCAT catalogue mirrors the DCAT-3 spec examples and wrote {"@id": ...}, which failed both layers -- while CDIF's own documented URI serialization policy (agents.md) says URI values SHOULD be {"@id": ...}. The register required the one form its own policy argues against.

properties.title: Method Name
properties.description: Short descriptive name with version (e.g. "JEOL-8530F WDS Major Element Glass v2.1").
DOI or other persistent ID for this method definition.
Human-readable summary of the method, may be auto-generated from constant parameters at registration time.
Semantic version string (e.g. "2.1.0").

properties.title: Method Start Date
properties.description: ISO 8601 date when this method configuration was first used.
ISO 8601 date of last update to this definition.

Further classification of the activity type (e.g. schema:CreateAction for a production method). A CURIE may also be written as a JSON-LD IRI reference, which is what CDIF's schemaorgProperties/additionalProperty SHACL asks for. This was the last of the eight sites in #77 still rejecting the @id form -- with it widened, the conversion probe goes from 344/345 to 345/345.

properties.title: Technique
properties.description: The analytical technique this method implements. Must be a DefinedTerm from a controlled vocabulary of techniques.
text label for the term that is useful to human user

The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.
A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

Target material(s) this method is designed to analyse (e.g. silicate glass, olivine, spinel), modeled as DefinedTerm(s) or free text; and/or the sample(s) analysed, modeled as iSamples material-sample objects (the "Samples analyzed" shape carried over from geochemProduct).

Instrument specification(s) for this method: a single instrument object, or an array of instruments when the method uses more than one (e.g. LA-ICP-MS = a laser ablation system plus the ICP-MS). Use schema:hasPart for instrument sub-components (spectrometers, detectors, ICP source, sample introduction system). Path-driven technique overlays select a specific instrument by schema:additionalType and constrain its sub-component tree.
Software tools used for data acquisition, reduction, and processing. Each tool carries name, version, and optional URL.
Reference materials, calibration standards, and chemical reagents used across this method. Reagents specific to a single workflow step should be placed on that step instead.

properties.title: Laboratory
properties.description: Laboratory where this method was developed. Optional; omit for methods that are instrument-generic.
Domain-specific type classifications for this place (e.g. facility type,laboratory classification, feature type).
A place name for the location, either as a string or a DefinedTerm from a gazetteer.
Formal identifier for this place (e.g. ROR identifier for a facility).
Alternate or abbreviated name(s) for this place.
Either a bounding box or a point location.

A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.

A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

Optional geographic extent using wkt geometry, see Ocean InfoHub (https://book.oceaninfohub.org/thematics/spatial/README.html#simple-geosparql-wkt). Other geometry schemes might be specified in a specific domain profile, e.g. for atmospheric, subsurface data, or local coordinate systems. NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.
identifier string for coordinate reference system, e.g., 'CRS84'

properties.title: Method Author
properties.description:
Person or organisation who defined or is responsible for this method.
The nested schema:description is OPTIONAL, and where present it records the PROVENANCE OF THIS DEFINITION -- how the TAPP definition itself came to be, as distinct from the method it describes. It is where a definition states that it was transcribed from a published protocol, derived from existing metadata records rather than authored by the laboratory, or produced automatically and reviewed by a person. A laboratory-authored TAPP needs nothing here; a draft assembled from other sources should not be mistaken for one, so it says so. The draft TAPP sidecars target it as the 'Procedure Author Description' row.
It sits on the creator rather than at the root deliberately: the claim is about who produced the definition and how, so it belongs with that agent, and a root-level property would invite a second copy. Note that the {'@id'} branch below is sealed, so a creator given as a bare reference cannot carry it -- a reference names an agent described elsewhere and makes no claim of its own.
The property is DECLARED by the person and organization building blocks this anyOfs, where it is a plain optional string. The note is here rather than there because those two blocks are general-purpose CDIF blocks with five other consumers, and this meaning is specific to a TAPP definition.

The standard workflow for this method, expressed as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action describing a distinct phase (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Steps carry their own parameters, reagents, instruments, and sub-steps. Exactly one step must be the sample-preparation step -- see MethodWorkflowHowTo.
Name of the workflow (e.g. "EPMA WDS analytical workflow").
Overview of the workflow.
URL to a published protocol document.

Ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action + schema:HowToStep describing a distinct phase of the analytical procedure. This shape carries NO sample-preparation requirement, because it is used for a STEP's sub-workflow as well as for a method's top-level workflow; see MethodWorkflowHowTo for the method form that does require one.
Name of this workflow step (e.g. "Sample preparation").
Detailed description of what this step involves.
Ordinal position in the workflow sequence (1-based).

Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for wet-lab steps, schema:CreateAction for production steps). A CURIE may also be written as a JSON-LD IRI reference, which is what CDIF's schemaorgProperties/additionalProperty SHACL asks for; the `contains` on the method's schema:step accepts either serialization, so widening here cannot orphan the sample-preparation requirement.
Instrument or equipment used in this step.
Software tools used in this step.
Reference materials, standards, or reagents used in this step.
Input entities consumed or referenced by this step (e.g. prepared sample from a prior step).
Output entity produced by this step (can be referenced as input by a subsequent step).
Reference to a prior step whose result is the input for this step (action chaining).

Step-specific parameters (e.g. beam conditions for the acquisition step, matrix correction settings for the data processing step). Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value.
Machine-readable parameter name for serialization (e.g. "acceleratingVoltage").
Guidance text shown to the user in the form.

Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).
The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.
true = constant, fixed for every session (read-only in form). false = editable (default or optional depending on valueRequired).
true = must be provided (mandatory). false = optional. Combined with readonlyValue: readonly+required = constant mandatory; !readonly+required = editable mandatory; !readonly+!required = optional.
Minimum allowed numeric value. Defines the lower bound of a valid range at the method level; specific values within this range may be set per element in ada:targetSpeciesTemplate.
Maximum allowed numeric value. Upper bound of valid range.
Granularity expected of the value (e.g. 0.1 for nA).
Regex pattern for validating string values.
Whether multiple values are allowed (default false).
Whether this parameter is fixed at the method level, varies per analytical session, or is element-specific.
Grouping label for form layout (e.g. "Beam Conditions", "Data Processing", "Quality Control"). String for simple cases; DefinedTerm to link to a controlled vocabulary of parameter categories.
Expected data type for the parameter value.
URI for unit of measure (QUDT preferred).
The CDIF building block property path this parameter maps to. Used for JSON-LD serialisation.
Mandatory / Recommended / Optional tier from the metadata profile. Informs validation strictness.
The fixed protocol value for this read-only parameter.

Sub-workflow for this step, expressed as a nested schema:HowTo with its own ordered steps. Use for steps that have a multi-phase internal procedure (e.g. sample preparation with mount, grind, polish, coat).
Quality measurements specific to this workflow step.

Method-level Advanced-protocol parameters that apply across all workflow steps. Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value. Replaces the former ada:methodParameters. Technique TAPP profiles constrain the allowed entries via $refs to the parameterTemplates (specifications) and parameterValues (values) registries. Step-specific parameters should be placed on the appropriate workflow step instead.

Template for per-target-material parameters, a target material being a material type this procedure is designed to analyse (Silicate mineral, Silicate glass, Oxide, Sulfide, Carbonate, Phosphate, Metal or alloy). Declares the target-material domain and the columns that repeat over it.
The domain is declared by the TAPP's Target Material field, marked `defines: target material`; the fields keyed BY it are the electron-beam conditions (Beam Current, Beam Mode, Beam Diameter, Beam Raster Dimensions, Beam Damage Minimization), and Primary Calibration Standard Name is keyed `target material x target species`.
Target materials are assumed present in any sample the procedure would analyse. The binding between a particular sampling unit and the material it hit is instance data, not procedure metadata, so it is recorded as a data-table column and NOT here -- this template carries only the kinds of material expected and the values that repeat over them.
Columns of the per-target-material parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "targetMaterial" that identifies the material named in each row.

The material types analysed, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose, and the counterpart of ada:targetSpeciesDeclaration: a submitter may name the materials as a list, or as prose that names none individually. ada:defaultTargetMaterials carries the members that could be recognised; this carries the statement they were recognised FROM, so a cell that parses only in part loses nothing.

The material types this procedure targets by default - the ROWS of the per-material table, and the domain `defines: target material` enumerates. An entry is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm naming the material, or a row object binding that material to per-material values.
A row object is keyed throughout by the schema:valueName of the columns declared in ada:targetMaterialColumns, and MUST carry the 'targetMaterial' key - the column that sibling description requires to identify the material named in each row.
Column-level constraints stay on the column: schema:readonlyValue when a value is constant across every material, and schema:defaultValue when one default serves the whole column. Use a row only for values that differ between materials.

Template for per-target-species (element-specific) parameters. Defines the columns that appear in the species table, each with scope, datatype, and constraints. Target-species rows become schema:variableMeasured entries in metadata records. Typically associated with the acquisition workflow step.
Columns of the per-target-species parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "targetSpecies" that identifies the analyzed constituent named in each row.

What this procedure analyses, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose, and the counterpart of ada:collectorConfiguration on the instrument side: submitters write the target species as a list, as a list with a sentence attached ("Mn (55Mn), Fe (57Fe) ... Pb (207Pb) in seawater"), or as prose that names no species individually at all ("Major and trace elements, masses 23-75"). ada:defaultTargetSpecies below carries the members that could be recognised; this carries the statement they were recognised FROM, so a cell that parses only in part loses nothing. Present whenever the declaration said more than the parsed rows record.

The target species (analyzed constituents) this method targets by default — the ROWS of the per-species table. An entry is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm naming the species, or a row object binding that species to per-species values.
A row object is keyed throughout by the schema:valueName of the columns declared in ada:targetSpeciesColumns, and MUST carry the 'targetSpecies' key - the column that sibling description requires to identify the constituent named in each row.
Which values belong here follows the TAPP's Analysis-Level Tier. A column marked Read-Only is fixed by the procedure, so its value belongs on the row. A column marked Editable takes a starting value here that an analysis may override; the value actually used is reported per result, as a column of the data table, and surfaces as schema:variableMeasured on the data product. Values that vary per result and are not defaulted do not belong here at all.
Column-level constraints stay on the column: schema:readonlyValue when a value is constant across every target species, and schema:defaultValue when one default serves the whole column. Use a row only for values that differ between target species.

Template for per-monitored-property parameters, a monitored property being an instrument selection position (a mass, a Faraday cup, an energy-loss edge, an X-ray line). Declares the monitored-property domain and the columns that repeat over it. The domain is declared by different fields per technique -- Monitored Isotopes for ICP-MS, Collector Configuration for MC-ICP-MS, EELS Edges for TEM.

Columns of the per-monitored-property table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "monitoredProperty" identifying the selection position named in each row. ("channel" was that name before the 2026-09 rename.)
A 'collector' column is the optional one worth knowing about: it maps each monitored property to the collector that carries it. That mapping is procedure CONFIGURATION, not instrument hardware -- the same array can be wired differently by another procedure, and an analysis may override it -- which is why it belongs here on the method definition and not on schema:instrument. The collectors themselves are hardware and live there, in hasPart[Collector].ada:collectors; this column's values are their schema:name.

Template for the variables this procedure REPORTS and their units, as distinct from ada:targetSpeciesTemplate which records what was acquired. Declares the reported-property domain and the columns that repeat over it. It also states the procedure's scope boundary: a derived quantity inside this list is in scope, anything beyond it belongs to a separate, coupled procedure.
Columns of the reported-property table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "reportedProperty" identifying the reported variable named in each row.

The reported properties this procedure defines by default — the ROWS of the reported- property table. Each is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm identifying the property; per-property column VALUES live in the analysis record, not here.
Quality measurements that characterize the method's expected performance (e.g. analytical precision, accuracy, counting statistics error). Uses the CDIF qualityMeasure building block.

properties.title: Method References
properties.description: Publications, Zenodo records, or other references reports describing or evaluating this method.
identifier for a particular grant
description of the funding or grant
title of the grant

properties.title: Reported Variables
properties.description: Variables / properties this procedure reports (e.g. detection limit, limit of quantification, calibration factor, uncertainty propagation method), each modeled as a schema:PropertyValueSpecification (a procedure-level default, carrying schema:defaultValue) or a schema:PropertyValue (a measured value, carrying schema:value), keyed by schema:name. A technique profile enumerates the reported properties it defines; a dataset instance overrides each schema:defaultValue with a schema:value. Left open here — the technique overlay narrows it.
Person(s) or laboratory responsible for developing and registering this procedure. ORCID recommended for individuals.
DOI or URL for peer-reviewed publications or technical reports describing, validating, or benchmarking this procedure.

Description of how this procedure is coupled with the technique(s) listed above. Include: (1) the functional relationship — what data or context flows between techniques, or how results are combined (e.g. which output from the coupled technique serves as input to data reduction for this technique); and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique is performed first and why (e.g. non-destructive before destructive). Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not "None".

The kind of physical subdivision of the sample to which one row of reported values corresponds — the unit that is analysed and reported, as distinct from the sample as a whole. Where units nest (e.g. confined tracks within grains), state both levels. The units themselves are listed in Sampling Unit Name.

The form in which the sample is presented to the instrument, and the preparation that brought it to that form — for example mounting, sectioning, polishing, coating, crushing, fusion, or extraction of an electron-transparent section. Record 'None' where the material is analysed as received.

An externally-calibrated factor that converts the measured quantity into the reported quantity, how it was determined, and its uncertainty. Applies where the conversion depends on a factor calibrated against a reference of independently known value, rather than on the instrument response alone. Distinct from the fields that name the calibration material and that state which approach applies to which target species, where the technique has them: this field records the resulting factor itself.
Acid mixture used for sample dissolution. Record acid type(s) and concentration(s) where known (e.g., concentrated HF–HNO3 in Parr bombs is standard for silicate dissolution).

Whether chromatographic separation of element groups (e.g., using ion exchange resin) was performed prior to analysis. Record resin type and elution matrix conditions if applied. Record 'None' if the direct digestion solution is analyzed.

Isotopic spike material added to the sample before or during digestion for isotope dilution (ID) analysis or double-spike mass bias correction. For double-spike procedures, add and equilibrate the spike before digestion. For concentration ID, the spike must be added before digestion for complete equilibration. Record spike name or certificate reference, spike isotopes, and whether added pre- or post-digestion. Record 'None' if ID or double-spike technique is not used.

Acid type and concentration of the final dissolved sample solution introduced to the instrument. For isotope-ratio procedures, match acid molarity precisely between samples and bracketing standards. Procedures targeting HFSE may add trace HF to the final solution to keep those elements in solution.
Duration of instrument rinse between successive sample solutions (seconds).

The convention at which reported uncertainties are quoted — 1-sigma, 2-sigma, or a 95% confidence interval — and whether a measured spread is reported as a standard error or a standard deviation. State the convention applying to all values reported under this procedure, and state each separately where different reported quantities use different conventions. Distinct from Uncertainty Propagation Method, which addresses how component uncertainties are combined rather than how the result is quoted.
Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).
Type of plasma torch installed (e.g. standard quartz, high-matrix, low-flow).

How often the primary calibration or bracketing standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session. Specify the bracketing scheme where a fixed one is used, such as one standard measurement before and after each sample.

Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. Record both the monitored mass ratio(s) and the maximum allowed threshold(s). Measured values are recorded in Oxide Production. The monitored ratio is procedure-dependent: ThO+/Th+ (m/z 248/232), UO+/U+ (254/238), CeO+/Ce+ (156/140) and BaO+/Ba+ are all in use.

Method used to subtract background and, where relevant, procedural blank from the measured signal. State what is subtracted - instrument background acquired with no sample reaching the plasma, an on-peak zero acquired on the same matrix, or a separately measured procedural blank - over what interval it is measured, and at what granularity it is applied.

Element(s) used as the internal standard, the monitored isotope, and how the internal-standard concentration was established for unknowns. Where the element serves isotope-ratio work it must have a known isotopic composition and a mass close to the target species's. Record 'None' together with the alternative used where no internal standard is applied.

Method used to define which portion of the acquired signal is integrated for each reported measurement, and the rule for excluding unstable or anomalous portions. State whether the interval is the full acquisition, a stable sub-interval selected by inspection, or selected by an automated criterion, and name the criterion.

The repeating order in which calibration or bracketing standards, quality-control and secondary reference materials, blanks and unknowns are interleaved within a measurement session. Adjustments must maintain the bracketing strategy defined in the procedure.
Formula or approach used to calculate the detection limits, with a citation for the method where one exists. Must be consistent with the values reported in Detection Limit.

Model designation of the instrument that performs the measurement, including any generation or configuration suffix. Conventionally written with the manufacturer name included; Instrument Manufacturer records the vendor separately, as a controlled value, so that procedures remain findable by vendor.

properties.const: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier

properties.description: Manufacturer of the instrument that performs the measurement, recorded as a controlled value. Where a procedure couples a sample-introduction system to an analysing instrument, this records the analysing instrument. Instrument Model gives the specific designation.

properties.title: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

properties.const: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

properties.title: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

properties.const: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

properties.title: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

properties.const: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

properties.description: Number of complete mass scans accumulated per analytical replicate. A scan — also called a sweep or a pass — is one complete traversal of the monitored masses by a sequentially scanning analyser, so the scan count multiplied by the per-mass dwell time gives the total integration time per replicate. Distinct from a cycle in simultaneous multi-collection, which is one readout of all detectors at once rather than a traversal of masses.

Number of replicate measurements performed on the same sample, or on the same nominal location where the technique is spatially resolved. For spot analysis this is the number of individual spots per grain or location; for transects, the number of replicate lines; for mapping, the number of map acquisitions of the same area; for solution work, the number of discrete replicate measurements acquired per sample solution.

Mode used to collect ion signal across the monitored masses. In peak hopping mode, the quadrupole jumps sequentially between pre-set mass positions and dwells at each peak; in scanning mode, the quadrupole sweeps continuously across a defined mass range.
Method used to correct for instrumental signal drift across a session.
Number of acquisition passes the procedure runs. A count of the passes enumerated in Acquisition Pass, recorded separately so multi-pass procedures are findable without parsing that field.
Human-readable display label (e.g. "Accelerating Voltage").
URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. Links to a skos:Concept or similar term definition. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).
Unit of measure label (e.g. "kV", "nA", "um").

The material type this row is for (e.g. "Silicate mineral"), from the controlled list the TAPP's Target Material field offers, optionally qualified in the same cell. The key is the schema:valueName of the identifier column, which ada:targetMaterialColumns requires exactly one of, so a row is keyed by column valueName throughout.

The analyzed constituent this row is for (e.g. "SiO2"). The key is the schema:valueName of the identifier column, which ada:targetSpeciesColumns requires exactly one of, so a row is keyed by column valueName throughout.
This key was 'analyte' until 2026-09-25. The rename moved the COLUMN's schema:valueName const to 'targetSpecies' but left the row half behind, so a row object could satisfy neither half: keyed 'analyte' it contradicted its own column, keyed 'targetSpecies' it failed this required. Nothing upstream caught it because every tappDefinition example lists bare strings here and so never exercises this branch; it surfaced against the 46 stored ADA method definitions, which do use row objects.
schema:name of the collector carrying this property, matching an entry in schema:instrument…hasPart[Collector].ada:collectors.
The species this property helps determine, when it determines one. Absent for a monitor.
The selection position measured, e.g. '⁸⁴Sr'. Becomes a schema:variableMeasured entry on the data product.
web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ
the identifier string. E.g. 10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.
Per-sample PropertyValue entries (e.g. analysis location); technique profiles constrain these.
Sample name/identifier as used in the lab.
Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.
Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.
Reference back to the instrument @id.
Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).

Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments), each naming how the target relates to the instrument. Uses the same linkRole block as cdifCore; before 2026-09-23 this property was a labeled link here and a LinkRole there.
The entry point being linked to. Deliberately not sealed: real targets also carry schema:httpMethod, schema:urlTemplate, schema:contentType and domain-specific properties, and JSON-LD is open-world.
registered MIME types are expected

How the target relates to the subject, as a controlled-vocabulary value or a plain string label. Required: a typed link whose relationship is unstated carries no more information than a bare URL, which is what schemaorgProperties/labeledLink is for.
Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.
Component type classification.

How masses are assigned to collector positions for this procedure, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose: submitters write this as prose or as a semicolon-separated list in no agreed syntax ("L3=116Sn (Sn); L2=117Sn (Sn); Ax=120Sn ..."), and in many cases it cannot be parsed at all. Recording the statement verbatim is what can always be done; ada:collectors below is what can sometimes be done as well. Meaningful on a component whose schema:additionalType includes 'Collector'.

The collector table. One member per position when ada:collectorConfiguration parses into positions, and ONE member carrying the text as written when it does not -- the N=1 form of the flattening fallback that TAPP-keyed-values-design.md Decision 6 settles for every keyed axis: "rather than admit two shapes, always emit the table: a declaration that does not parse into members yields a one-row table whose row key is the text as written. The fallback is then not a separate branch but N=1."
So a consumer reads one shape either way. In the N=1 form schema:name is a fixed label rather than a cup ('Collector configuration description'), schema:description carries the unparsed string, and the per-item values ride in schema:additionalProperty as name/value pairs. Parsing these strings to individual collectors is not tractable in general -- they are written for a person to read -- so N=1 is expected to be the common case, not the exception.
This exists because a cup label has to be referenceable WHEN there is one. A per-cup quantity (a baseline, a gain factor) and a monitored property that names the position reporting it both need something to point AT, and a label buried in a sentence is not something a consumer can join to. schema:name is that anchor.
What a collector does NOT carry is which monitored property it measures. That assignment is procedure configuration, not hardware -- the same physical array is wired differently by another procedure, and an analysis may override it -- so it lives as the 'collector' column of ada:monitoredPropertyColumns on the method definition, whose values are these schema:names. Putting it here would invert the dependency and make the instrument description procedure-specific.
Note what an N=1 member does NOT assert: it names no cup, so it makes no per-cup claim. That matters because the resistor values are attested per MASS, not per cup (Proposal_Monitored_Property_2026-09-10 §10), and the fallback must not quietly move them onto the collector axis.

The collector position label as the instrument names it -- L5..L1, C or Ax, H1..H5, IC1..IC8 on a Neptune-class multicollector. This is the identifier other properties reference. In the N=1 fallback there is no position to name, so it is the fixed label 'Collector configuration description' and nothing should join to it.

Quantities carried on this member as name/value pairs. In the parsed form these are per-position quantities that cannot be restated per mass -- a baseline, a gain factor. In the N=1 form they are the source fields themselves, each as its item name and the text as written, which is how an unparseable per-collector statement is preserved without inventing an assignment it does not make.
The item name, e.g. 'Faraday Cup Amplifier Resistor Values'.
The value, as written when it did not parse.
Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.
Date the instrument was commissioned (ISO 8601).

Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.). On a procedure / plan instrument (e.g. an instrument named directly on an ada:TAPPDefinition) these are schema:PropertyValueSpecification parameter templates (an overridable default); on a prov:used analysis-event instrument they are schema:PropertyValue concrete values. The JSON Schema accepts both; a profile SHACL rule pins which form applies in which context.

A value fixed by the procedure, where the parameter is NOT overridable. Both keys are declared because both occur: measured across the geochemBuildingBlocks corpus on 2026-10-09, of 369 PropertyValueSpecification entries under schema:instrument, 203 carry schema:defaultValue and 166 carry schema:value. A specification that pins a value rather than defaulting one is still a specification.
Human-readable label for the parameter.
Guidance text for the parameter, e.g. shown beside a form control.

The overridable default this specification carries -- the value that applies unless the analysis overrides it. Left untyped: a default may be a string, a number or a boolean, and which one is a property of the parameter rather than of this shape.
Machine-readable name for the parameter, for serialization and for binding a form control to it.
identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.
